method: Same Chromium 155, 1280x800 viewport, cloud SwiftShader software renderer. Short forward-walking sample after startup; timing includes browser scheduling and software rasterization. V3 performance preset versus V4 Low. These are different scene contents and short samples, not a controlled hardware benchmark.

baselineV3.renderer: SwiftShader software (cloud, not target desktop GPU)

finalV4.renderer: SwiftShader software (cloud, not target desktop GPU)

comparison.interpretation: Software rendering remains the bottleneck. The final sample is about 2% slower than V3; no FPS improvement is established. Earlier V4 samples varied around 0.8–0.9 seconds/frame. New visual/gameplay work fits within similar cloud rendering cost, but this is far below playable frame rates on this software-only machine.

cpuAndScene.note: CPU values are the last telemetry sample, not average or tail-latency guarantees. Render submission time is not GPU execution time. Rolling in-game frame statistics also include startup warmup; use the separate frame-sample fields for the walking comparison.

optimizations: Material/geometry batching and instancing preserve original GLB textures, vertex colors and extra UV channels.
Bounded grass LRU cache, velocity-biased queue and 1.6ms generation budget.
Actual oak/alder model impostors and movement-threshold instance updates.
Prebuilt/frustum-culled terrain sections with matching physics.
Nearest-three pooled local lights; scalable cascaded shadows, AO and planar water refresh.
Low disables shadows, reflections and postprocessing and lowers resolution/vegetation.
limits: No target Mac or Brave hardware-GPU benchmark was available. Stable 60 FPS is unverified.
High/Ultra render correctness was tested; their hardware frame rates were not measured.
Brief samples are sensitive to warmup and cloud scheduling; do not interpret small differences as a performance gain.
